raw_response:
Well, let me think about this year the way I always do. I'm an old man now — 70 years — and my wife and me, we work these 6.8 mu the same way I learned from my father and have done my whole life. Nothing fancy.

I've got 4 mu in the good flat ground where I do the wheat and then maize straight after — that's the pattern everyone around here does, and I've been doing it for decades. The other 2.8 mu, closer to the edge of the village, I keep in cotton. It's dirty work picking cotton at my age, but cotton gives you cash in hand when you sell it, and we need some cash for the year.

**Wheat first, because that's what's going in the ground first this fall and it's always on my mind.** I'll put it in around the ninth lunar month, early October by the new calendar, after I clear the maize stalks. I buy seed from the grain station in town — just the regular kind everyone plants, I don't pay for the fancy named varieties. I never went to school, I can't read the bags, I just point at what they sold me last year. Before planting, I spread one bag of the compound fertilizer on each mu — that's the "三个十五" kind with the three numbers on it, the blue bag. Then when the wheat comes up in spring and starts jointing, if it looks pale I scatter maybe half a bag of urea per mu. If the color looks okay, I save some urea. My eyes have seen a lot of wheat — I know when it needs feeding. I'll water it three times if the sky doesn't help — once before the ground freezes, once at jointing, once when the grain is filling out. The well water costs electricity money so I don't waste it. For the harvest I pay the combine man who drives through the village, it's 40 or 50 yuan a mu, can't do it by hand anymore, my back won't take it.

**Maize goes in straight after the wheat combine leaves the field**, no time to rest the ground, you have to hurry — maize likes a long summer. I hire the neighbor with the no-till planter to run through, 30 yuan a mu, he drops the seed and the fertilizer together. I must buy hybrid seed every year, maize seed you can't save, everyone knows that. I put one bag of compound at planting, and when it gets to the big flare stage — when it's taller than me and about to tassel — I put urea around the roots, maybe half a bag per mu. I might water once or twice if July turns dry. Mostly our summer rains are enough.

**Cotton is the hard one.** I plant late April after the cold passes. The seed I buy at the market, the shopkeeper tells me what's good, I trust him, he's been there twenty years. Cotton eats fertilizer but I don't give it too much because then it grows all leaves and no bolls — my grandfather taught me that. Maybe one bag of compound per mu and a little urea later. Cotton wants spraying — bollworms, aphids, all that. I spray a few times with whatever the agro-shop tells me to use. The picking is the thing. My wife and I go out every morning in September and October and pick, pick, pick. Our daughter comes back from town for a few days to help. 2.8 mu is about what the two of us can still manage. More than that I'd have to hire pickers and the price isn't good enough to pay them.

**Money.** I have to watch every yuan. My son sends a little but mostly we live off what we grow and sell. If the fertilizer shop raises prices I use less. If the cotton price is bad I might put that land in maize next year. But for now, same as last year — that's been working.
